hints.title: Store history per key
hints.body: One global list is not enough: a read only cares about writes to its own key. Keep a separate timestamp history for every key.

hints.title: Append without sorting
hints.body: Writes are globally increasing in time, so each key's history is automatically sorted. Appending a new write preserves that order.

hints.title: Binary search the cutoff
hints.body: For a query time `t`, find the rightmost recorded timestamp less than or equal to `t`. If none exists, the answer is the empty string.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
history = empty map from key to list of (time, value)
answers = empty list
for each operation:
    if operation is set: append (time, value) to history[key]
    else:
        list = history.get(key)
        if list is missing or empty: append "" to answers
        else:
            find rightmost index i with list[i].time <= query time
            append list[i].value if i exists else "" to answers
return answers
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete solution.
